clue.text: Hides, having slept out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of slept are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been sleeping rough, out in the open, with only animal skins for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal skins with the fur still on are called by this word, a synonym for hides.

clue.text: American author and man of letters

explanation.surface: A literary American and a writer of letters described together.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Mailer was an American novelist; read literally, a 'man of letters' is someone who sends post, a mailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer is the novelist; a person who posts letters is literally one who mails them.

clue.text: Part-time reporter on his beam-ends?

explanation.surface: A freelance journalist who has hit hard times and is down on his luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On his beam-ends' is an idiom for being broke, but here it points to a stringer as a long structural beam in a ship or staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance journalist paid per piece is called this; also a longitudinal timber in a hull or stair.

clue.text: Pert young woman in certain cases

explanation.surface: A cheeky young woman who is described only in particular situations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In certain cases' reads as 'sometimes', but it means things carried in suitcases: luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned term for a cheeky girl, and also luggage packed in suitcases.

clue.text: Tyneside town welcome to Berliners

explanation.surface: A town in north-east England with a greeting for visitors from Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallsend is a town on the River Tyne where Hadrian's Wall ends; the fall of the Berlin Wall, a wall's end, was welcomed by Berliners.
explanation.definitionFit: The town takes its name from the eastern end of Hadrian's Wall; Berliners rejoiced at the end of their own wall in 1989.

clue.text: Grouse about giant pram

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters of giant pram are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a huge baby carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like a verb meaning complain, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain bird is a member of the grouse family, white in winter.

clue.text: Acted as front runner misguidedly?

parts.note: a leader who went ahead badly might be said to have headed the wrong way; the phrase also means misguided others

explanation.surface: A race leader who took the field off in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in pieces: having acted as front runner is having been in front, and misguidedly is off course; together the phrase means deceived or corrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means misguided or corrupted, here pictured as a leader going the wrong way.

clue.text: Roundabout way to settle for a meat pie

indicators.note: roundabout tells us the words to settle sit around the word way

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Advice to take a detour on the road in order to get a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' looks like a traffic island or a detour, but it is a container signal. A pasty is a pastry turnover associated with Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish pasty is a folded pastry case filled with meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Just fine

explanation.surface: A two-word remark meaning merely all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just fine' reads as one phrase but splits into two senses: equitable, and sunny weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable treatment is just; dry pleasant weather is fine.

clue.text: Following scout leader in conversation

indicators.note: the leader of scout is the letter at its head, its first

explanation.surface: A youth group leader is being followed while deep in chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout leader' suggests a person, but it means the first letter of 'scout'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalking means following someone stealthily, as a hunter tracks prey.

clue.text: Charm of a river, on the whole

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another means it comes after it

parts.note: the whole means all of it
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river that, all things considered, is charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the whole' looks like the phrase 'generally', but it splits: in an across clue 'on' means placed after. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm and attraction are synonyms of this noun.

clue.text: Give oneself a pat on the back for card game

definitions.text: Give oneself a pat on the back

explanation.surface: Someone congratulating themselves at a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Brag is an old British card game, an ancestor of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to praise oneself; it is also the name of a three-card gambling game.

clue.text: Evergreen shrub flowering in poor drainage

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of drainage are in bad order and must be reworked

explanation.surface: A plant blooming despite waterlogged soil.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant white-flowered bush is an evergreen.

clue.text: Signs of a small worker?

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Questioning what the signals of a little labourer might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs' suggests indications, but it means symbols, as in a stenographer's script.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of abbreviated symbols for writing quickly, as taken by secretaries.

clue.text: His turn to be very cold

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist given to the letters of His

explanation.surface: It is his go now, and he feels very chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His turn' reads as 'his go', but 'turn' scrambles HIS to SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling chilled enough to tremble; shivering from cold.

clue.text: Spiteful enough to waste a number at the outset

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals, placed at the start of the answer
to waste away is to perish

explanation.surface: Someone so nasty they would squander a number right at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: VI is the Roman numeral six; 'waste' in the sense 'waste away' gives PERISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous and malicious, like a snake's bite.

clue.text: Scornful response to a sizeable offer?

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a generous proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: As an exclamation it dismisses something as unimportant; literally it is a large transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Said sarcastically it means 'so what?'; literally a large business transaction.

clue.text: One whose work could be of patent interest

definitions.text: One whose work could be of patent interest

parts.words: One whose work could be of patent interest
parts.note: patent reads as obvious, but means the legal protection given to a new device

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is plainly interesting.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who devises new machines would register a patent on them.

clue.text: Covering a point in transvestite wear

indicators.note: in puts the words a point inside the clothing

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex worn for performance
a pin has a sharp point

explanation.surface: A drag artist pinning up the outfit to cover themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' is clothing of the opposite sex; PIN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging cloth loosely over something is covering it.

clue.text: He offers to support Rose in trouble

parts.note: to prop something is to support it

indicators.note: in trouble suggests Rose is disturbed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A man offers to help Rose, who is in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' is a woman in the surface, but her letters become OSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who puts forward a motion at a meeting offers it for a vote.

clue.text: Say nothing about the sauce

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about the sauce, someone is told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say nothing' reads as 'keep quiet', but 'about' mixes the letters of SAY with O.
explanation.definitionFit: A soy-bean condiment, often used as the name of the sauce itself.

clue.text: Sell a number at the finish

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Selling one item right at the very end of the sale.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman numeral five.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to sell, as in a vending machine.

clue.text: Nullify what could be neat, for example

indicators.note: could be suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters given

explanation.surface: Wondering what might cancel out tidiness, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' tells you to rearrange NEAT together with EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel out or invalidate something is to render it void.

clue.text: Sound resentful in a tangle

explanation.surface: Growling angrily while caught up in a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it is to growl angrily; as a noun it is a knot or muddle, as in a traffic snarl-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl of anger, and a knotted mess or traffic jam.

clue.text: Lively sound of cricket on the third of May

parts.note: the insect's noise is a chirp

indicators.note: the third of points to the third letter of the word May, not a date

explanation.surface: The noise of a cricket match on the third day of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' suggests the sport; it is the insect. 'The third of May' looks like a date but means May's third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful and bright, like a chirping bird.

clue.text: Elusive king-pins of the spirit world

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for drinks that belong among spirits

indicators.note: elusive suggests the letters of king-pins slip away from their places and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ghostly leaders who escape capture in the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit world' suggests ghosts but means alcoholic spirits; 'Elusive' asks for an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin flavoured with bitters is a cocktail belonging to the family of spirits.

clue.text: Worry about gnats

indicators.note: about here means the letters of gnats are moved around

explanation.surface: Fretting over a swarm of small insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling of dread or anxiety, a German loanword.

clue.text: Roving Argonauts' contribution to 26

indicators.note: roving means wandering, so the letters of Argonauts' wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Wandering Greek heroes add their share to the earlier entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to 26 across: bitters of this name are what turns gin pink.
explanation.definitionFit: These aromatic bitters are the ingredient that colours a pink gin.
